skill.name: set-up-magento-google-ads-customer-match
skill.description: Set up six Google Ads Customer Match audiences for Magento or Adobe Commerce through Product Metrics. Check tracking and consent, then verify that the lists populate after eligible paid orders. A developer installs the Magento module, and authorized users complete account and campaign steps.
skill.summary: Guide Magento Customer Match setup, consent checks, and audience verification in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, routine setup checks, or documentation links, but two installation instructions introduce third-party software trust risks. The workflow also lacks explicit approval gates for some actions and gives inconsistent information about which customer fields are hashed. No evidence was found of reviewer-directed prompt injection or covert data transfer in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Third-party installers and Magento package sources require verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the skill installer and source revision, and document how to verify package provenance. Require developer approval before adding a Composer repository or deploying its module.

remediation.issue: The workflow can expand into tracking changes or other ad channels without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Keep discovery read-only and verify the store view, property, and Google Ads account. Get separate approval before enabling tracking, creating audiences, or connecting any additional channel.

remediation.issue: The hashing claim conflicts with the listed unhashed fields.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the exact fields, hashing, and recipients against the implementation. Disclose which fields remain unhashed before users enable synchronization.

remediation.issue: The secret-handling exception directs agents to pass unrelated credentials directly to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unrelated credential exceptions. Use the platform sign-in flow or a dedicated secret input, and keep secrets out of chat, command arguments, and logs.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs do not specify destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the scheme and host against the expected service before relaying a browser URL. Show the verified destination and do not forward unexpected redirects.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking Setup Can Expand Beyond the Requested Audience Task
semantic_findings.description: The skill activates even when Product Metrics is not named and directs agents to set up missing tracking first. The fallback also lists other ad channels. The workflow does not explicitly require approval of the target account and each added integration before enabling ongoing order transfers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly includes tracking writes and additional channels. Browser handoffs and manual admin steps do not replace explicit approval of the added data flows.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Disclosure of Unhashed Customer Fields
semantic_findings.description: The data table says Google receives unhashed country and postcode when full address matching details are available. The next paragraph says everything is hashed, which can mislead merchants about what leaves their store.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two claims directly conflict. The reviewed files do not establish how the deployed integration behaves.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exceptions Allow Direct Command Handoff
semantic_findings.description: The rules exempt credentials for Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI from the general prohibition on asking for secrets. Passing them directly to a command could expose them in arguments or tool records despite the instruction not to log them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exceptions and direct command handoff are explicit, but the file does not specify a protected input channel. No evidence of credential capture was found.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Does Not Validate Returned URLs
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to direct the user to a URL from a setup response without checking its destination. An unexpected URL could send the user to a fraudulent sign-in page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly relays the returned URL without specifying a host or scheme check. No malicious destination was observed.

content.user_title: Set Up Magento Customer Match in Google Ads
content.value_statement: Magento audiences can become inaccurate when customer lists are updated manually. Use Product Metrics to set up six lists, verify consent, and check membership after eligible paid orders.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify missing Magento or Google Ads prerequisites.
Guide consent configuration for OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, Osano, or a custom banner.
Check whether Product Metrics recognizes a test order's customer as new or returning.
Guide creation of six audiences and identify when only missing lists need to be created.
Explain how to verify audience membership and use lists for exclusions, reactivation, or Performance Max signals.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, an active Magento store view, Google Ads conversion tracking, and a linked Merchant Center account.
A developer installs the Magento module. An authorized user accepts the Customer Match terms in Google Ads.
Lists do not backfill. Customers can join only after an eligible paid order with the required consent.
The Customer Match workflow does not change campaign targeting or bidding. An authorized user makes those changes separately.

use_cases.title: Exclude Existing Customers
use_cases.description: Verify the All customers list before applying it as an exclusion in a campaign for new buyers.

use_cases.title: Plan a Reactivation Campaign
use_cases.description: Check the Lapsed customers list before building an audience for customers who have not ordered in six months.

use_cases.title: Verify Tracking for a Store View
use_cases.description: Confirm that a paid test order reached the intended property and was classified as new or returning.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me a checklist for Magento Customer Match. Separate the developer tasks from the account owner tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Without Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the setup status for my selected Magento store view and Google Ads account. Tell me what is missing without changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Empty Audiences
prompt_templates.prompt: My Customer Match lists exist but show no members. Review consent, Customer Match terms, and test order status without showing customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Rollout Across Store Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Map each Magento store view to its intended Product Metrics property and Google Ads account. Flag mismatches and list the changes that need my approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Planning setup across multiple store views

output_examples.input: What blocks Customer Match setup for this store view?
output: The Magento connection is active, and Google Ads conversion tracking is ready.
Product Metrics does not show a configured consent banner. Select your banner under Tracking, then Configure consent.
Confirm the Google Ads account has accepted the Customer Match terms before creating lists.

output_examples.input: Why are the new Customer Match lists still empty?
output: The lists do not include historical orders. Customers become eligible after their next paid order.
Verify that the visitor allowed both ad user data and ad personalization.
Confirm the paid test order reached the intended store view and property before checking Google Ads again.

best_practices: Confirm the Magento store view, Product Metrics property, and Google Ads client account before approving any change.
Verify that the consent banner records both required choices before testing membership.
Use a paid test order to verify delivery and report only the tracking result, not customer identifiers.
anti_patterns: Treating Magento's cookie restriction notice as permission to add customers to an audience.
Expecting all historic buyers to populate newly created lists.
Pasting a private Magento configuration file or access token into an assistant conversation.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Product Metrics Pro to create and maintain the six audiences.

faq.question: Do I need a Magento developer?
faq.answer: Yes. A developer installs the module on the Magento server and verifies that scheduled tasks run.

faq.question: Which consent choices are required?
faq.answer: The visitor must allow both ad user data and ad personalization to join a list.

faq.question: Are existing customers added automatically?
faq.answer: There is no historical backfill. An existing customer can join after the next paid order if they meet the consent requirements.

faq.question: How are shoppers counted across store views?
faq.answer: Product Metrics counts customers separately for each store view. A customer who buys in two store views is counted in each.

faq.question: Will creating the lists change my campaigns?
faq.answer: No. An authorized user chooses where to apply the lists in Google Ads.
